title: Training Notes on the Prompt-Pay Rate for Charges Enrolled in Patient Payment Plans
content:
Patient Services Center training notes on the prompt-pay rate kept by a charge posted for an encounter already enrolled on a proposed Patient Payment Plans plan.

**Q. When does such a charge keep a prompt-pay rate?**
A. A charge enrolled no more than the prompt-pay window of the patient's Patient Financial Account, in calendar days after its posting date, keeps a prompt-pay rate when the plan pays by automatic debit: the account's full prompt-pay discount percentage when the plan's automatic debit method is ACH, and half of it when the method is card or HSA/FSA card. With no automatic debit, or once more than the prompt-pay window's days have passed since posting, the prompt-pay rate is 0.

**Q. Whose figures are these?**
A. The prompt-pay window (in calendar days, counted from the charge's posting date) and the prompt-pay discount percentage are the figures the financial class of the Patient Financial Account sets.

**Q. How does the rate act on the amount enrolled?**
A. The remaining balance of the charge is multiplied by one minus the prompt-pay rate divided by 100, without intermediate rounding.

| Days from posting to enrollment | Automatic debit method on the plan | Prompt-pay rate |
|---|---|---|
| No more than the account's prompt-pay window | ACH | The account's full prompt-pay discount percentage |
| No more than the account's prompt-pay window | Card or HSA/FSA card | Half of the account's prompt-pay discount percentage |
| No more than the account's prompt-pay window | None | 0 |
| More than the account's prompt-pay window | Any | 0 |

**Q. Where is the edge of the window? (hypothetical 30-day window)**
A. A charge posted on 1 March and enrolled on 31 March is enrolled 30 days after posting, no more than the window, and keeps the rate; enrolled on 1 April, 31 days have passed and the rate is 0.

**Q. What does a hypothetical figure look like?**
A. With a class prompt-pay discount percentage of 10.00 and a remaining balance of 300.00: by ACH inside the window the rate is 10.00 and the balance is multiplied by 0.90, giving 270.00; by card inside the window the rate is 5.00 and the balance is multiplied by 0.95, giving 285.00.
